s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of a painless swelling over a pacemaker site with a soft tissue mass and increased vascularity surrounding the device
salient_findings: Painless swelling over the pacemaker site
Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity on chest ultrasound
CT imaging confirmed a soft-tissue mass around the pacemaker pocket
key_facts: 70-year-old man with a history of nicotine use
Remote history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Remote history of bladder urothelial carcinoma
Dual-chamber pacemaker implantation for sick sinus syndrome 9 months prior
Postoperative checks showed normal pacemaker function
Clinically unremarkable pocket at 3 months
Tested positive for COVID-19 infection 3 weeks prior to presentation
Fatigue, dyspnea, and cough persisted and worsened after COVID-19 infection
New swelling over the pacemaker site reported at a routine cardiology visit
Normal blood pressure and heart rate on examination
No signs of cardiac decompensation or cachexia
Haematoma or infection excluded by imaging

shortlist.label: Metastatic laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma and new swelling over pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Metastatic bladder urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of bladder urothelial carcinoma and new swelling over pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device

shortlist.label: Primary soft tissue sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of a painless swelling over a pacemaker site with a soft tissue mass

shortlist.label: Pacemaker-related fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: New swelling over pacemaker site and history of pacemaker implantation

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma and presents with a new, painless swelling over the pacemaker site, which imaging reveals to be a solid, vascular mass, suggesting a malignant process.

rejected.label: Metastatic bladder urothelial carcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of bladder urothelial carcinoma, the presentation and imaging findings are more suggestive of a metastasis from the laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence to suggest angiosarcoma, such as rapid growth or extensive vascular involvement.

rejected.label: Primary soft tissue sarcoma
rejected.why: The patient's history of cancer and the appearance of the mass make metastasis more likely than a primary soft tissue sarcoma.

rejected.label: Pacemaker-related fibroma
rejected.why: The mass is described as solid and vascular, which is not typical of a fibroma, and the patient's history of cancer makes a malignant process more likely.
